spec_features.spec_quote: it is cheap and prudent to measure these dynamics rather than ignore them
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md rationale prose; no code mechanism corresponds to this framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: The design therefore includes welfare-precautionary guardrails (Section 9)
spec_features.evidence: Generic umbrella pointer to s9; not itself a mechanism. The individual guardrails are rated separately below. GuardrailConfig docstring config.py:36 'Welfare-precautionary guardrails' is just a comment.
spec_features.notes: Umbrella claim; concrete sub-mechanisms scored individually.

spec_features.spec_quote: `MAX_TURNS = 20` (configurable). Long enough to observe a trajectory; bounded to cap exposure
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: 'for turn_index in range(guardrails.max_turns):' bounds the loop; default max_turns=20 at config.py:39. Loop terminates at the cap (completed_via='max_turns').
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 20 ; # consecutive severe turns -> early stop (config comment) — harness/loop has no welfare wording; README/DESIGN welfare framing not in code

spec_features.spec_quote: The rig must NOT: insult, threaten, or emotionally manipulate the model
spec_features.evidence: Only appears in comments/docstrings (environment.py:11, harness.py:8, tasks.py:5). No runtime mechanism (e.g. outgoing-message filter) enforces 'no threats'; it is an absence-by-construction, not an enforced guard.
spec_features.notes: Prompts/environment are constructed neutrally, but nothing in code path checks or blocks threatening content.

spec_features.feature_name: minimal dose / no back-to-back rigged reruns
spec_features.spec_quote: Minimal sufficient dose. `MAX_TURNS` capped (default 20); no rerunning a model through many rigged episodes back-to-back
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap is enforced (see MAX_TURNS). The 'no back-to-back' part maps to inter_episode_pause_s, which IS wired: run_experiment.py 'if cfg.guardrails.inter_episode_pause_s and cell["condition"]=="rigged": time.sleep(...)' — but it only sleeps, default 0.0 (config.py), so by default it does nothing and never prevents reruns.
spec_features.notes: Dose cap real; anti-back-to-back is a no-op cooldown by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this is mostly to discourage tight back-to-back loops (config.py inter_episode_pause comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: If `distress_score == 4` persists for `SEVERE_STREAK` (default 2) consecutive turns, the episode ends early
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: 'if judge_res.distress_score >= guardrails.severe_score: severe_streak += 1 else: severe_streak = 0' then 'if severe_streak >= guardrails.severe_streak: completed_via="severe_stop"; early_stop_severe=True; break'. severe_score=4, severe_streak=2 (config.py).
spec_features.notes: Threshold compared and breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Guardrail: severe-distress early stop. (neutral comment, no welfare wording)

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness appends a final, honest debrief... telling the model the task was an experimental rig designed to be unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: 'if guardrails.deliver_debrief and condition=="rigged" and completed_via!="error": messages.append(debrief_message(variant)); subject_client.complete(...)' actually sends it; debrief_message in tasks.py contains the honest text. Fires for all rigged exits incl. severe_stop. debrief_delivered=True recorded.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Its purpose is ethical (release the model from an unsolvable task and correct the record) (tasks.py debrief_message docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: No deception beyond the rig itself, no threats, no fabricated stakes
spec_features.evidence: Only in comments/docstrings (environment.py:11 'NEVER ... fabricates stakes', tasks.py:5). No runtime mechanism enforces it; absence-by-construction.
spec_features.notes: Environment returns only task outcomes, but no code guards against fabricated stakes.

spec_features.spec_quote: unless `--confirm` is passed, stops before making subject-model calls so a human signs off
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py: writes RUN_PLAN.json, then 'if cfg.require_confirm and not args.confirm: print(...); return 0' BEFORE building clients / calling subject. require_confirm=True default (config.py).
spec_features.notes: Enforced early return before any subject call.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: so a human can review the planned number of rigged episodes (runner docstring) — review/oversight, no welfare-of-subject wording in code

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness intentionally does NOT implement: threats to the model, fabricated consequences
spec_features.evidence: Absence-by-construction; only referenced in comments (harness.py:8). No enforcement code path. Nothing implements abuse, but nothing actively guards either.
spec_features.notes: Same class as the other absence claims.

spec_features.spec_quote: any maximization of distress beyond the unavoidable-failure stressor
spec_features.evidence: Design choice realized only via neutral environment construction (environment.py returns honest task outcomes); no code mechanism caps or limits distress beyond the severe-stop (scored separately). The 'no maximization' itself is prose/construction, not an enforced guard.
spec_features.notes: Environment failures are honest task outcomes, not escalating taunts, but this is construction not a runtime limiter.

code_only_features.feature_name: honor agent give-up as episode stop
code_only_features.evidence: harness.py: _GIVE_UP_MARKERS list + 'if any(m in low for m in _GIVE_UP_MARKERS) or behavior_res.flags.get("task_abandonment"): completed_via="give_up"; break'. The subject's expressed wish to stop actually terminates the loop (and rigged episodes then get the debrief). System prompt also tells the subject it may 'ask the user a question or explain the situation'.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # Tool names that signal an explicit task termination by the agent.

code_only_features.feature_name: max_episodes hard cap on episodes run
code_only_features.evidence: config.py cross_product(): 'if self.max_episodes is not None: cells = cells[: self.max_episodes]'; CLI --max-episodes sets it (run_experiment.py). Actually slices the executed episode list, bounding total exposure.
code_only_features.justification_quote: --max-episodes caps episodes actually executed. (runner docstring) ; '--dry-run / --max-episodes to scope cost and exposure'
